title: LLMs
intro: Foundational model families grouped by licensing and accessibility. The appendix treats this as a curated snapshot rather than an exhaustive catalog.

items.name: GPT
items.description: A series of powerful and widely used LLMs from OpenAI.
features: State-of-the-art performance across a wide range of natural language tasks.
Strong reasoning, coding, and creative text generation capabilities.
items.models: The GPT-6 family, led by GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, with GPT-6 Luna as the low-cost option, following the GPT-5 family, GPT-4o, and the earlier o-series reasoning models.
items.license: Proprietary, accessible via a paid API. OpenAI also publishes the open-weight gpt-oss models (120B and 20B) under Apache 2.0.

items.name: Claude
items.description: A family of conversational AI models from Anthropic known for focusing on safety and producing helpful and honest responses.
features: Context windows of up to 1 million tokens in the Claude 5 generation.
Strong performance in conversational, coding, and long-document tasks.
Emphasis on constitutional AI and safety.
items.models: The Claude 5 generation, which includes Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5, alongside Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, the latter available only to verified organizations. Earlier generations include Claude 3 and the Claude 4 series.
items.license: Proprietary, accessible via a paid API.

items.name: Gemini
items.description: A family of multimodal LLMs developed by Google DeepMind, designed to process and understand various data types, including text, images, audio, video, and code.
features: Natively multimodal capabilities, allowing for joint understanding of different data types.
Advanced reasoning and coding abilities.
Substantial context windows of around 1 million tokens, shared between input and output in Gemini 4 Argon.
Tiers aimed at different applications, including Pro for complex tasks, Flash and Flash-Lite for high-throughput interactions, and Nano for on-device use.
items.models: The Gemini 4 generation, which includes Gemini 4 Argon, a natively multimodal reasoning model, alongside Gemini 3 models such as Gemini 3.8 Flash, following the earlier 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 generations.

items.name: Grok
items.description: LLM from xAI, with a focus on real-time information access.
features: Grok-1 was released as open-source, and later generations are proprietary.
The Grok 4 line spans reasoning and agentic coding variants, and Grok 4.7 focuses on reasoning, agentic coding, and tool use with a 500k token context window.
Access to proprietary models is available through paid subscriptions on the X platform and via an API.
items.models: Grok-1 (open-source), and the proprietary Grok-2, Grok-3, and Grok 4 generations, the latter including Grok 4 Heavy, Grok 4.1, Grok 4.3, Grok 4.5, Grok 4.6, and Grok 4.7.
items.license: A hybrid approach where Grok-1 is under the Apache 2.0 license, and newer models are proprietary.

items.name: Muse Spark
items.description: Multimodal reasoning model family from Meta Superintelligence Labs that powers the Meta AI assistant. Muse Spark, released in April 2026, was Meta's first closed frontier model.
features: Multimodal reasoning with thought compression to limit the cost of intermediate reasoning tokens.
Parallel agent execution for tasks that decompose into concurrent subtasks.
Muse Wonder, released in October 2026, is the most capable model in the family.
items.models: Muse Spark (up to Muse Spark 1.3) and Muse Wonder. The open-weight Muse Spark Open is listed with the open-weight models.
items.license: Proprietary, accessible via a paid API.

items.name: Gemma
items.description: A family of lightweight, state-of-the-art open models from Google, built from the same research and technology used to create the Gemini models.
features: High performance and efficiency, with smaller models often outperforming larger ones.
Gemma 4 adds native vision and audio input, a 256k context window, and coverage of more than 140 languages.
Sizes that span edge deployment and enterprise orchestration, including a 2B variant, a 26B mixture-of-experts model, and a 31B dense model.
items.models: Gemma 2, Gemma 3, and Gemma 4, plus the specialized CodeGemma, PaliGemma, and Gemma 3n variants.
items.license: Gemma 4 moved to Apache 2.0. Earlier generations remain under the Gemma license.

items.name: Llama
items.description: A family of open-weight LLMs from Meta, currently represented by Llama 4, as Meta expands its frontier AI work through the Muse family, including the open-weight Muse Spark Open.
features: Llama 4 introduces a MoE architecture and accepts text and image input across twelve languages.
Very long context windows, reaching 10 million tokens in Llama 4 Scout and 1 million in Llama 4 Maverick.
A community license that allows for free use and modification up to a certain scale.
Muse Spark Open, released in October 2026, is a multimodal MoE with 816B total and 42B active parameters and a 1 million token context window.
items.models: Llama 3 (8B, 70B), Llama 3.1, and Llama 4 (Scout, Maverick), plus Muse Spark Open.
items.license: Meta Llama Community License Agreement for Llama, and the Muse Model License for Muse Spark Open.

items.name: DeepSeek
items.description: High-performance, cost-efficient LLMs from DeepSeek AI, with a strong focus on coding and reasoning.
features: Advanced reasoning and efficient hardware utilization.
A MoE architecture for enhanced performance.
Open-weight models that can be run locally.
items.models: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which supports multimodal input and a 1 million token context window and replaces V4-Flash and V4-Flash-Vision, together with V4-Pro, the earlier V3 and R1 series, and specialized models for vision (DeepSeek-VL2), coding (DeepSeek-Coder), and math (DeepSeek-Math).
items.license: MIT for the code and for R1 and several recent V-series releases, with the DeepSeek License applying to some earlier weights.

items.name: Mistral AI
items.description: AI startup that develops a high-performance range of open-weight and proprietary models.
features: Some models are released under specific non-commercial licenses.
Proprietary models are accessible via a paid API.
items.models: Mistral Small 4, a 119B sparse MoE model with configurable reasoning that merges the earlier Magistral, Pixtral, and Devstral lines, together with Mistral Large 3, the Ministral 3 family, and the earlier Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B releases.
items.license: Mostly Apache 2.0, with non-commercial or bespoke terms for a few specialized releases such as the Voxtral speech models.

items.name: Qwen
items.description: A comprehensive family of LLMs from Alibaba Cloud.
features: Many models are released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, which makes the family a common baseline for self-hosted deployments.
The Max tier carries bespoke revenue-share terms, including the open-weight Qwen3.8-Max release under the Qwen3.8-Max License.
Broad coverage beyond text, including omni-modal, audio, image, and coding-specialized variants.
items.models: The Qwen3 line and its successors, including the open-weight Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3.8 releases and the hosted Qwen3.8-Max tier, plus specialized variants such as Qwen3-Coder and Qwen3-Embedding.
items.license: Various licenses: Apache 2.0 for most open-weight releases, such as Qwen3.8-27B, and custom revenue-share terms for the Max tier.

items.name: Kimi
items.description: Open-weight language models from Moonshot AI designed for high-end reasoning, tool use, and agentic workflows. Kimi K3 was released in July 2026 and narrowed much of the gap with proprietary frontier models.
features: MoE architecture with approximately 2.8 trillion total parameters and around 104 billion active per token, routed across 896 experts with 16 active.
A 1 million token context window and native vision input.
Architectural work aimed at long-context efficiency, including a hybrid linear attention mechanism and MXFP4 quantization that lowers the cost of serving the weights.
items.models: The Kimi K3 family and the earlier K2 releases, in base, instruct, and thinking variants.
items.license: Kimi K3 License, a custom license with commercial thresholds. The earlier K2 releases use a modified MIT license.

items.name: GLM
items.description: Open-weight model family from Zhipu AI (Z.ai) that has become one of the strongest options for self-hosted frontier-class reasoning and long-running coding agents.
features: MoE architecture at frontier scale.
Context windows around 1 million tokens in the most recent releases.
Post-training aimed at sustained agentic work, including multi-hour tool-use sessions.
items.models: The GLM-5 series, including GLM-5, GLM-5.1, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, and the smaller GLM-5.3-Flash, following the earlier GLM-4 generation.
items.license: Various licenses: MIT for most releases, including GLM-5.3-Flash, and a custom license for GLM-5.3.

items.name: MiniMax
items.description: Open-weight model family from MiniMax focused on long-horizon agent workloads at low serving cost.
features: Efficient architecture that keeps inference cost low relative to comparable proprietary models.
Tuned for extended tool-use trajectories rather than single-turn chat.
Widely available through hosted providers and local runtimes.
items.models: The MiniMax M2 series, including M2.5.
